nodes.label: D-001 v1 covers protests only
nodes.rationale: Redress hearings have a different form and flow; building both at once doubles surface before either is proven.

nodes.label: D-002 Product entirely in English
nodes.rationale: Racing rules' defined terms are native to English and carry exact technical meaning that does not survive translation.

nodes.label: D-003 Single user, local first, no accounts in v1
nodes.rationale: The owner is the only user; accounts/roles/permissions are the classic sink for personal projects that will 'one day' be multi-user.

nodes.label: D-004 Nothing is cited unless it is in the corpus
nodes.rationale: A language model citing rules from memory invents numbering with total confidence; a misquoted rule is a badly founded decision.

nodes.label: D-005 No .docx export in v1, copy-paste per box
nodes.rationale: Export was the least valuable and most tedious block of work and carried a library licensing question that no longer needs answering.

nodes.label: D-006 Editor: CodeMirror 6, TipTap rejected
nodes.rationale: TipTap's Content AI requires a paid subscription and reserves custom LLM backends for the business plan; this project uses Claude, self-hosted. CodeMirror covers both suggestion mechanisms in one engine at no cost.

nodes.label: D-007 Three separate material stores: rules, examples, phrases
nodes.rationale: They have different levels of trust; a user phrase must never be presented as a rule, an example must never be cited as authority.

nodes.label: D-008 The rules corpus is layered, with precedence
nodes.rationale: Sailing instructions and amendments modify the RRS; citing the RRS while ignoring an event amendment yields a citation that is correct and a decision that is wrong.

nodes.label: D-009 Everything is stored as Markdown
nodes.rationale: One format for the AI to read, one format for the index, no per-format branching in code.

nodes.label: D-010 No OCR
nodes.rationale: OCR is a heavy dependency inside the container; the user's workflow already handles it externally.

nodes.label: D-011 SQLite, not Postgres; FTS5, not a vector database
nodes.rationale: One user, one writer; SQLite needs no container/administration. Parsing RRS by rule number and keyword search is more precise and cheaper than embeddings at this corpus size.

nodes.label: D-012 Built to be containerised from day one
nodes.rationale: Rules like env-var config, data under one directory, 0.0.0.0 binding and configurable TZ are free now and painful later.

nodes.label: D-013 File sync exclusions (.stignore)
nodes.rationale: Real-time sync over thousands of small files corrupts repos, and syncing a live SQLite file mid-write corrupts the database.

nodes.label: D-014 Rules Applicable stored as a separate table
nodes.rationale: Rules Applicable is a hybrid (free text now, validated against corpus later); a table survives that transition without migration.

nodes.label: D-015 Table named protest_case, not case
nodes.rationale: CASE is a reserved SQL keyword; using it as a table name forces quoting everywhere and invites mistakes.

nodes.label: D-016 SQLite access via node:sqlite, not better-sqlite3
nodes.rationale: better-sqlite3 failed to compile (no Visual Studio C++ toolchain); node:sqlite ships with Node itself and needs no native compilation.

nodes.label: D-017 Copy-per-box covers all 8 form sections
nodes.rationale: 'Writing assistance' is narrower than 'copy to clipboard'; the whole document gets pasted into the official decision one piece at a time.
